title: Korean Fried Chicken Thigh Nuggets with Gochujang Glaze
summary: Bite-size boneless thigh pieces cured with salt, MSG and ginger, battered and dredged in potato starch, double-fried and tossed in a sweet, tangy gochujang-garlic sauce.
notes: Video: 'The Best Korean Fried Chicken At Home' on the Joshua Weissman Recipes channel (UCUAg71CJEvFdOnujmep1Svw). Written recipe: https://www.joshuaweissman.com/recipes/the-best-korean-fried-chicken-at-home-recipe (serves 4, prep 20 min, cook 30 min; it says to make either the wings or the popcorn chicken, or both, from one batch of sauce, dredge and batter). The video makes both versions from that one batch, so the video is split into two recipe files (wings and nuggets) and the shared sauce, dredge, batter and frying lines are repeated in each. Sauce: tossed on the chicken and made in a bigger batch than goes on it (he calls it a big batch, uses it for both versions and says to use as much or as little as you like); no share is stated, so 50% of the batch is counted in each file (house rule 10; the full batch is about 2 2/3 cups). The garlic is strained out of the sauce (his recommendation), so it is not counted. Honey is listed as the alternative to rice syrup and not counted. Rice syrup uses a malt-syrup proxy and dark soy sauce uses regular soy sauce. Sweet soy sauce grams use our 1.25 g/ml estimate. Coatings: dry dredge 25% and wet batter 50% (house rule 3); because 1/3 cup of the dredge goes into the batter, each dredge ingredient counts at 27.6% (arithmetic in each line). The couple of tablespoons of batter flicked into the dredge for crunchy bits are ignored. Gram weights for starch, flour and MSG are the written recipe's. The 1-inch knob of ginger is our estimate of 10 g (his jerk chicken recipe weighs a 3-inch knob at 31 g). Frying oil: about 3 quarts in the video (the page says 2-3 quarts of canola or peanut oil; canola, named first, is used); the pot is excluded and absorbed oil is counted at 10% of the raw coated weight (house rule 2), using the as-bought weight. Times are the written recipe's hands-on prep and cook; the cure (at least 1 hour, ideally overnight) is not in prep_minutes (house rule 13). Nuggets: about six boneless, skinless thighs in the video (the page says 6, about 2 lb / 908 g); counted as 6 thighs at USDA's 149 g. Cure grams for MSG (2 g) and salt are the written recipe's. The video says the nuggets get the same batter, dredge, double fry and sauce as the wings, so those lines repeat the wings file. The written recipe lists 3 green onions for the popcorn chicken too (counted) and toasted sesame seeds, which the video does not use on the nuggets (left out). Absorbed oil: raw weight is 6 x 149 = 894 g thighs plus 22 g of cure (5 g salt, 2 g sugar, 2 g MSG, 3 g pepper, 10 g ginger) plus 213.1 g of coating. Bite-size pieces probably carry more coating per gram than wings; the fixed house shares are used anyway.

steps.text: Sauce: in a small saucepan, stir together the gochujang, rice syrup, dark soy sauce, vinegar, sweet soy sauce and ketchup. Boil over medium-high heat for 2-3 minutes to reduce.
Mince the garlic finely. With the heat completely off, stir it into the sauce (never boil it). Let it steep 5-10 minutes, then strain the garlic out.
Cut the boneless thighs into bite-size pieces; there is no need to trim the fat.
Cure: toss the pieces thoroughly with the kosher salt, sugar, MSG, grated ginger and black pepper so every piece is evenly seasoned. Use right away, or refrigerate at least an hour or overnight.
Dry dredge: whisk the potato starch, flour, salt, sugar, MSG, garlic powder and white pepper together.
Wet batter: whisk 1/3 cup of the dredge with the baking powder, then whisk in the cold water. Optionally flick a little batter into the dredge for crunchy bits.
Dip the pieces in the batter, press them into the dredge until fully coated, and set them on a sheet tray.
Fry the same way as wings: first at 325°F in about 3 quarts of oil until cooked through (they cook quickly), then again at 350°F until golden and crisp. Drain on a rack.
Toss the hot nuggets in the sauce until completely covered, pile them high in a bowl, and top with green onion.
